rewrites.//: SPA fallback for genuinely dynamic routes (/exam/:id, /live/:code, /dashboard). Vercel checks the filesystem BEFORE applying rewrites, so the per-route files written by scripts/prerender.mjs — dist/blog/<slug>/index.html and friends — are served directly and never reach this rule. Do not narrow it: any route without a prerendered file still needs it.

headers.//: The prerendered documents (dist/blog/<slug>/index.html etc.) are requested at extensionless paths, so the /index.html rule above never matches them. Without this they could be edge-cached with a stale head and a content update would not surface. The negative lookaheads keep this off /assets and off anything with a file extension, so the immutable asset rules above stay in force.

Private routes, hardened at the transport layer. X-Robots-Tag is obeyed by crawlers that never fetch robots.txt and by those that ignore it, and unlike a meta tag it does not depend on the HTML being parsed. This is the third of three layers: server-side RPC authorisation is what actually stops an attacker, the first-byte noindex meta covers HTML consumers, and this covers everything else. Listed by path here rather than in robots.txt because vercel.json is build config and is never served to visitors.
